This small piece of land, less than a quarter of my farm, I use for yam — it is food for my family and what remains I can sell in the market. The soil here is tired from last season, so I will put a small bag of NPK to help the yams size up, and also spread the manure from my goats before I make the mounds. I save my own seed yams from last harvest, as we always do, and I will spray once against the grasshoppers and weeds because hoeing alone cannot keep up. My wife and children and I will do most of the work, but making the mounds and staking is heavy, so I will call two or three young men from the village to help me for some days.
